title: Sriram Balaji Has Reached His First Grand Slam Quarter-Final. He Is Thirty-Four. He Did It at Roland Garros.
excerpt: India's Balaji and Brazilian partner Marcelo Demoliner stunned sixth seeds Krawietz and Puetz in straight sets to make the French Open doubles last eight.
body:
Sriram Balaji has been playing professional tennis for over a decade. He has represented India in Davis Cup ties. He has ground through Challengers and Futures across continents. On Monday, at thirty-four years old, he reached the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam for the first time in his career.

Balaji and his Brazilian partner Marcelo Demoliner defeated sixth seeds Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 7-5, 6-4 in the men's doubles fourth round at the 2026 French Open, setting up a quarter-final clash against second seeds Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten.

## The Comeback from 0-2 Down

It did not start well. The Indo-Brazilian pair fell behind 0-2 in the first set against the formidable German duo. But Balaji and Demoliner broke back in the third game and then held their nerve through a series of tight service games.

The first set hinged on the eleventh game. With the score at 5-5, Balaji and Demoliner broke Krawietz-Puetz's serve to take a 6-5 lead, then closed out the set 7-5 with a comfortable hold.

The second set was more clinical. A break in the opening game gave the unseeded pair an early cushion they never relinquished, winning 6-4 to wrap up a straight-sets victory over opponents ranked significantly higher.

## India's Doubles Tradition

For Indian tennis, doubles has often been the more reliable path to Grand Slam glory. Leander Paes won eight Grand Slam men's doubles titles. Mahesh Bhupathi claimed four. Sania Mirza dominated women's doubles and mixed doubles for the better part of a decade. Rohan Bopanna won the Australian Open mixed doubles title in 2024 at the age of forty-three.

Balaji fits into a different tier of the Indian doubles pipeline — not a household name, not a perennial Grand Slam contender, but a steady, committed professional who has quietly improved his game year after year. Reaching a Grand Slam quarter-final at thirty-four, after years of anonymity on the lower tours, is the kind of late-career breakthrough that Indian sport rarely celebrates but should.

## What Is Next

The quarter-final against second seeds Heliovaara and Patten will be the toughest test yet. The Finnish-British pair are among the most consistent doubles teams on tour and will enter as heavy favourites on the Philippe Chatrier clay.

But Balaji and Demoliner have already exceeded expectations. For a player who has spent the better part of his career on the Challenger circuit, every round at Roland Garros is uncharted territory — and the kind of story that rarely makes front-page news in India but means everything to the athletes living it.

## The NRI Connection

Balaji's run coincides with another Indian milestone at this year's French Open. Indian-American Nishesh Basavareddy — whose parents emigrated from Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, in 1999 — upset seventh seed Taylor Fritz in the men's singles earlier in the tournament. Between Basavareddy's diaspora breakthrough and Balaji's professional perseverance, the 2026 French Open has been quietly significant for Indian tennis.

*Balaji and Demoliner face Heliovaara/Patten in the quarter-finals on Tuesday or Wednesday. The French Open concludes on Sunday, June 7.*
author: Diaspora Desk
